13.08.2025 WPMB No. 563 of 2025
with
WPMB No. 474 of 2025
Hon’ble G. Narendar, C.J.
Hon’ble Alok Mahra, J.
1. Mr. Navneet Kaushik, learned counsel for the 
petitioners in both the cases.
2. Ms. Rajni Supyal, learned Brief Holder for the 
State of Uttarakhand. 
3. Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned CGSC for the Union of 
India. 
4. Mr. Ramji Srivastava, learned counsel for the 
National Commission for Indian System of Medicine.
5. Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel for Dev 
Bhoomi Medical College of Ayurveda & Hospital.
6. Learned counsel for respondent no. 5-University 
was directed to secure instructions, regarding the 
correctness of the action of the University in denying 
publication of results and issuance of mark-sheets. 
Today, the learned Standing Counsel for the University 
would submit that he has been instructed by the 
University to state that, pending final decision by the 
State Government, the University would be publishing 
the results only. 
7. The piecemeal approach by the University is yet 
again no surprise to this Court. The University has 
been playing along with the Management and the 
Colleges, who have thrown all caution to the winds, 
and despite an earlier order imposing penalty of 50 
lakhs and regularizing admissions, the University has  turned a blind eye to the continued transgressions by 
the Management, who have admitted students, and 
whose admissions we do not know, as to whether they 
are sanctioned by the University, or by the Competent 
Authority or by the State Government, and such 
students have been permitted to take up examinations 
on an yearly basis, and every time the students would 
approach this Court, and this Court would direct the 
publication of results and issuance of mark-sheets.
8. The above narration would, prima facie,
demonstrate that the University is probably hand in 
glove and in all probability, the management must be 
acting in connivance with certain officials of the 
University, making a mockery of the University’s Acts, 
Statutes and Rules. This charade is probably being 
played over and over again just to gain a stamp of 
legality to the nefarious activities of the vested 
interests. It is apparent that the students have 
become a pawn in the hands of these vested interests. 
9. Be that as it may, the fact remains that the 
students have taken up the examinations conducted by 
the University, and today the approach of the 
University, in our prima facie opinion, is condemnable. 
Having conducted the exams on the one hand, trying 
to withhold the results on the other hand, the 
University is trying to play the character of Jekyll and 
Hyde, which, in our opinion, is not an action that can 
be called as a fair one. Having knowingly conducted 
the exams, and the students having prepared and 
worked hard, and having successfully completed the 
exams, a right should be inferred in favour of the 
students to have the results and fruits of such efforts 
given to them. 10. In that view, the University shall publish the 
results and also issue the marks-card, as some of the 
students have even cleared the NEET PG Examination 
for the MD Course. In that view, the results shall be 
published within a week, and the marks-card shall be 
issued within a week thereafter.
11. This issue of the students being forced to take 
examination, and then being compelled to approach 
the Courts, is something this Court does not 
appreciate. The issue of illegal admissions, and 
managements and colleges making illegal money is a 
larger issue that requires to be addressed.
12. Hence the instant Writ Petition is directed to be 
converted into and registered as a PIL. 
13. Registry shall take action accordingly. 
14. List these cases on 08.09.2025.
 (Alok Mahra, J.) (G. Narendar, C.J.) 
 13.08.2025 13.08.2025

Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Gupta, C. J.

1. Mr. Navneet Kaushik, learned counsel for the 
petitioners.
2. Mr. J.C. Pandey, learned Standing Counsel with 
Mr. M.S. Bisht, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned Standing Counsel for 
the Union of India.
4. Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel for 
Uttarkhand Ayurveda University.
5. Mr. Ramji Srivastava, learned counsel for 
National Commission for Indian System of Medicine. 
6. The present writ petitions relate to students 
who were admitted to BAMS Course in different 
institutions in the academic year 2018-19. This 
Court, vide its order dated 26.02.2020 in WPMS 
No.2911/2018, filed by an association of private 
unaided educational institutions in Uttarakhand in 
the name of Association of Combined Entrance 
Examination, permitted the University to consider 
the case of 474 students of the said academic year 
for enrollment, subject to payment of ₹ 50.00 lakhs 
as penalty by the petitioner association. 
7. It is stated by learned counsel for the 
petitioners that the association had duly complied  with the said condition and had deposited ₹ 50.00 
lakhs with the respondent University. In the 
aforesaid backdrop, it is urged that the students who 
have been admitted are entitled to appear in the 
examination and their result be declared but time 
and again the University is creating hindrance in the 
same.
8. Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel 
appearing on behalf of the respondent university 
does not dispute that ₹ 50.00 lakhs was deposited
by the association with the University in terms of 
order dated 26.02.2020 in WPMS No.2911/2018. He, 
however, submits that the petitioners are not
amongst the 474 students, who were permitted to 
be enrolled by this Court. He states that he will 
provide list of 474 students, who were permitted to 
be enrolled, to learned counsel for the petitioners 
within two days. 
9. Accordingly, he is permitted to provide the list 
to learned counsel for the petitioners, so that they 
may complete their instructions on the said aspect. 
10. Let these petitions be delinked from the 
bunch and be listed separately on 07.05.2026.
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)
